1) Concrete monthly examples that show how streaming audio-to-text / streaming chat sessions would be converted to billable tokens (we're worried about rounding when sessions send lots of small partial updates).
2) How commit tiers and true-up interact with streaming sessions across multiple regions (we have US & EU workloads — will usage aggregate under the same commit or be region-separated?).

I've attached a small workbook with sample traffic patterns. Can you respond with a short plain-language explanation and a contract-friendly clause we can pass to legal?

Sara — thanks for the clear asks and for the workbook. Looping in Marissa (SE) and Laura (billing). Below I’ll summarize the high-level approach, then Laura will propose contract text and Marissa will add the technical rounding examples.

High-level summary (plain language):
- For interactive streaming (chat and streaming audio-to-text), we meter per-token generated and per-token consumed by the model. In streaming, we count tokens when they are emitted from the model; short partial updates are still billed as the tokens the model returned, there is no per-chunk minimum beyond token granularity.
- Rounding policy: tokens are counted exactly (integer count) — we do not round up to fixed-size chunks (e.g., 1KB). For streaming that produces many tiny emits, each emitted token is billed; however, the runtime includes micro-batching and prefix caching which reduces duplicated token generation.
- Commit tiers: commits are aggregated at the account level by default (your HubSpot account / customer id). By default, cross-region usage (US + EU) will count toward the same commit unless you request region-isolated metering in the contract.

Marissa — can you paste the small examples from the workbook (chat session, streaming audio with partial transcripts) and a one-line explanation of batching impact?

Laura — can you draft a 2–3 sentence contract clause and a short example table (monthly usage, billable tokens, price applied) for procurement/legal?

Thanks all —
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Sara — quick technical examples, copied from your workbook and simplified: 

Example A — Short chat session with partial updates\- 1 user opens session, sends 3 short turns (5, 7, 6 tokens)\- Model emits incremental streaming tokens: 4 partial emits (2, 3, 6, 7 tokens) as it finalizes each turn\- Billable tokens = total tokens emitted by the model across the session = 2+3+6+7 = 18 tokens. User input tokens are billed separately if you choose to bill inputs; our pricing by default bills both input and output tokens, but we can provide an input-exempt configuration for server-side safety review.

Example B — Streaming audio-to-text with partial interim transcripts\- 1 minute audio with interim emits every 5s resulting in small partial transcripts (avg 10 token interim, final 50 tokens)\- If interim emits are 10+10+10+20 (partial) then final 50, billable tokens = sum of emitted transcripts = 100 tokens.

Batching/optimization note: our runtime will micro-batch concurrent streams and de-duplicate repeated prefixes via KV cache; this reduces billable tokens when you send repeated prompts or rehydrate old context. It does not alter the counting rules (we still count actual emitted tokens), but it lowers overall emissions in practice.

Let me know if you want me to compute the three workbook scenarios against their proposed commit ladder and add a CSV (I can attach pricing_examples.csv).

—Marissa

Subject: Proposed contract language: billable units + commits

Hi Sara / Procurement team — please find a short, contract-oriented clause below. This is intentionally concise for legal review; Hannah, flag anything you want changed.

"Billable Units. For the purposes of charges under this Agreement, a \"billable token\" means a discrete token emitted by Redwood's model runtime or submitted as model input. Tokens are counted as integer units at the time they are emitted or received by the runtime. Interim streaming emits (e.g., partial transcripts or partial chat deltas) are billable in the period they are produced. Redwood does not apply fixed-size rounding buckets for token billing; the billed quantity is the aggregate integer token count.

Commit and True-Up. Customer commit tiers shall apply to the aggregate billable tokens associated with Customer's account ID. By default, usage across regions (e.g., US and EU) aggregates against the commit. If Customer requires region-isolated metering, the parties will execute an addendum specifying separate commits per region. Customer will receive a monthly true-up invoice for usage exceeding the committed tier; unused committed units will not roll forward unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Sample pricing table (illustrative):
- Month usage: 12,450 billable tokens — Price applied: tier 1 at $0.000012/token
- Commit: 10M tokens/month reserved — True-up: 12,450 charged at overage rate

Attachments: Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)

If these sentences look good I can prepare a redline to your MS Word PO or integrate into your SOW.

Thanks,
Laura

Laura — quick drafting suggestions from legal so the clause is clearer on proration and audit rights: 

1) Add a sentence: "Charges shall be prorated for any partial billing periods for new commits or contract term adjustments."
2) Clarify audit window: "Customer may request usage audit evidence (logs and token counts) within 60 days of invoice issuance; Redwood will provide supporting metering logs subject to confidentiality and redaction of other customers' data."

Suggested tweak to the roll-forward sentence above: "Unused committed units will not roll forward unless expressly stated in an addendum; any roll-forward or carry-forward mechanics shall be negotiated at contract execution."

Happy to produce a marked-up clause for your counsel.

—Hannah
